description: Managed over herd health management of research animals and diverse undergraduate and graduate students
Development and management of livestock facilities: Nutrition and Health
Collect and process field data, laboratory procedures, and various administrative tasks as needed to meet objectives of ruminant research projects
Conduct educational lectures, demonstrations, and tours to outreach programs for extension agents, small farm producers, community, and elementary and secondary school districts.
Prepare purchasing requisitions, invoices and purchase orders materials and services
Assist with results of research proposals and evaluation of livestock research development programs.
Assisted in tutoring 4-H students in various clubs for upcoming competitions

Assisted with decorating and photographing several program activities for 4-H
Judged at the beef and sheep expo skill-a-thon contests: retail cuts, breeds, feeds, medication, and parts of the animal Assisted with livestock evaluation and showmanship of county 4-Her's

matchmaking_summary: This candidate possesses a strong educational background in agriculture and extension, with specific expertise in youth development and adult advocacy. With experience as a research assistant manager and involvement in various community projects, they demonstrate excellent analytical skills, organizational abilities, and project management skills. Their ability to mentor and educate effectively has been evident through leadership roles within multiple organizations, particularly in the context of 4-H programs. The candidate's ability to adapt educational methods to meet the needs of diverse audiences highlights their flexibility and commitment to professional development.
